glosses: To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.

examples.text: The earthquake destroyed several apartment complexes.
Hooligans destroy unprovoked.

glosses: To neutralize, undo a property or condition.

examples.text: Smoking destroys the natural subtlety of the palate.

glosses: To put down or euthanize.

examples.text: Destroying a rabid dog is required by law.

glosses: To severely disrupt the well-being of (a person); ruin.

examples.text: Her divorce destroyed her; she had a nervous breakdown and was severely depressed for more than a year.

examples.text: Remember when Germany destroyed Brazil 7–1 in the World Cup?

examples.text: The memory leak happened because we forgot to destroy the temporary lists.

glosses: To exhaust completely and thus recreate or build up.

examples.text: This exercise is going to destroy all parts of your shoulders.

glosses: To penetrate sexually in an aggressive way.

examples.text: She got destroyed by her lover on the carpet.

glosses: To sing a song extremely poorly.

glosses: To eat food quickly, hungrily or completely.

examples.text: I could destroy some wings right now.

glosses: To crush or dash to pieces.

examples.text: The whales / Against sharp rocks, like reeling vessels, quashed, / Though huge as mountains, are in pieces dashed.
